correctness.rationale: A standard zero-endpoint Brownian bridge split at t in (0,1), conditional on signed B_t=x, consists of two independent Brownian bridge legs of lengths t and 1-t. The classical endpoint local-time survival exp[-(z²+2|x|z)/(2u)] for each leg yields the explicit two independent exponential representation for L|R_t=r, with each summand strictly decreasing in r, proving negative regression and all bounded increasing transform covariance inequalities (strict under the stated nondegeneracy). Independently, occupation density gives E[L|B_t|]=integral_0^1 p_{B_s}(0) E(|B_t||B_s=0)ds; Gaussian conditional variance splits at s=t and beta/trigonometric integration gives sqrt(t)+sqrt(1-t)-1. From EL=sqrt(pi/2) and E|B_t|=sqrt(2/pi) sqrt(t(1-t)), the exact covariance factorizes -(1-sqrt(t))(1-sqrt(1-t)). This is strictly negative, maximal magnitude at t=1/2, and Fubini gives all L1 deterministic weighted areas with constant-weight 1/3-pi/8. Independently evaluated Gaussian split integral by high-precision quadrature at t=.11,.25,.5,.8, agreeing with formula; continuum proof is analytic.
